description: Guard invalid-config persistence server-side (F-4 correctness slice) and centralize + atomicize the config-number generator (Q-3). ProductConfigurator::saveConfiguration() persists selections even when validation is invalid; two duplicated, racy generateConfigNumber() implementations compute CFG-{year}-{count+1}. No UI/UX niceties (Phase 3). Independent of the engine features; depends on FEAT-001 factories for tests.
steps: In ProductConfigurator::saveConfiguration(): after $result = evaluate(...), if $result->validation['valid'] === false, REFUSE to persist — do not create the ConfigurationSession or its items/BOM; surface a validation error (session flash or Livewire error) and return. Rationale: configuration_sessions.status allows only draft/validated/finalized (see WorkspaceController::updateStatus in:draft,validated,finalized), so there is no 'invalid' status to persist; refusal is the correct guarantee. A valid configuration must still save exactly as today.

Create app/Services/Configuration/ConfigurationNumberGenerator.php with 'public function next(): string' returning CFG-{year}-{6-pad} (match the current format). Make it collision-safe: run inside a DB transaction, derive the next sequence for the current year (max/count with lockForUpdate), and on a unique-violation QueryException retry in a bounded loop. The configuration_number column is already unique() (migration 2026_10_06_030000) and acts as the backstop — no new index required.

Replace ProductConfigurator::generateConfigNumber() and WorkspaceController::generateConfigNumber() with calls to the shared generator (inject via constructor or app(ConfigurationNumberGenerator::class)). Keep the produced format identical.

Add tests/Feature/InvalidConfigSaveTest.php (Pest, Livewire::test(ProductConfigurator::class, ['product'=>$product])): a config missing a required visible attribute (or selecting a disabled option) creates NO ConfigurationSession row and surfaces an error; a valid config still creates the row. Add tests/Feature/ConfigurationNumberTest.php: generating N numbers yields N distinct values; inserting a duplicate configuration_number throws a unique-constraint error. Run Pint and targeted tests, then the full suite.
acceptance_criteria: An invalid configuration cannot be persisted via saveConfiguration(); no partial/inconsistent ConfigurationSession is created (InvalidConfigSaveTest passes).
A valid configuration still saves with its items and BOM as before.
Both call sites use one shared ConfigurationNumberGenerator; the CFG-{year}-{6pad} format is unchanged.
Generating many numbers yields distinct values and the unique constraint rejects duplicates (ConfigurationNumberTest passes).
No existing Phase 0/1 test regresses; full suite green.
findings:
DONE. Full suite green: 46 passed (110 assertions), including the 5 new tests (InvalidConfigSaveTest 2 + ConfigurationNumberTest 3). No Phase 0/1/earlier Phase 2 regressions.

=== Invalid-config guard (app/Livewire/Configurator/ProductConfigurator.php) ===
saveConfiguration() now evaluates first; if $result->validation['valid'] === false it sets $this->result = $result->toArray() (so the UI still reflects the evaluated state), calls $this->addError('configuration', <message>), and RETURNS before any persistence. No ConfigurationSession, items, or BOM rows are created for an invalid config. A valid config saves exactly as before (session + items + bomItems, then redirect to configurator.show). The old private generateConfigNumber() was removed.

=== Shared generator (app/Services/Configuration/ConfigurationNumberGenerator.php) ===
New class with 'public function next(): string' returning CFG-{year}-{6-pad} via sprintf('CFG-%d-%06d', ...) - identical format to both old implementations. Collision-safe: derives the sequence inside a DB::transaction() using ConfigurationSession::withTrashed()->whereYear('created_at',$year)->lockForUpdate()->count()+1, then re-checks the candidate is not already taken (withTrashed) and retries in a bounded loop (MAX_ATTEMPTS=5) on a taken candidate or QueryException; throws RuntimeException if it cannot resolve. withTrashed() is used because configuration_number is unique across soft-deleted rows too (the unique index is the backstop). No new migration/index added (configuration_number already unique() in migration 2026_10_06_030000).

=== Both call sites unified ===
ProductConfigurator::saveConfiguration uses app(ConfigurationNumberGenerator::class)->next(). WorkspaceController now injects ConfigurationNumberGenerator via constructor property promotion and uses $this->configurationNumberGenerator->next() in duplicate(); its private generateConfigNumber() was removed. Format is byte-identical between both paths.

=== Tests (tests/Feature/) ===
InvalidConfigSaveTest.php: Livewire::test(ProductConfigurator::class, ['product'=>$product]) with an empty selection against a required+visible attribute -> assertHasErrors('configuration') and ConfigurationSession::count() === 0; a valid selection -> assertHasNoErrors(), one session created with one item and configuration_number starting 'CFG-{year}-'. Seeds RolesAndPermissionsSeeder and acts as a 'sales' user.
ConfigurationNumberTest.php: 10 generated+persisted numbers are all distinct; format matches /^CFG-\d{4}-\d{6}$/ and starts with CFG-{year}-; inserting a duplicate configuration_number throws QueryException (unique constraint). Pint clean.
